arxiv-2012-06406.title: Reducing subspaces of C 00 C_{00} contractions Thanks: This work was partially supported by Labex CEMPI (ANR-11-LABX-0007).
arxiv-2012-06406.creator: Chafiq Benhida, Emmanuel Fricain, Dan Timotin
arxiv-2012-06406.description: Abstract . Using the Sz.-Nagy–Foias theory of contractions, we obtain general results about reducibility for a class of completely nonunitary contractions. These are applied to certain truncated Toeplitz operators, previously considered by Li–Yang–Lu and Gu. In particular, a negative answer is given to a conjecture stated by the latter. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 47B35,47A15,47B38 1.

arxiv-2012-13857.title: Two-dimensional topological superconductivity candidate in van der Waals layered material
arxiv-2012-13857.creator: Jing-Yang You, Bo Gu, Gang Su, Yuan Ping Feng
arxiv-2012-13857.description: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) topological superconductors are highly desired because they not only offer opportunities for exploring novel exotic quantum physics, but also possess potential applications in quantum computation. However, there are few reports about 2D superconductors, let alone topological superconductors.

arxiv-2101-04171.title: Maximizing Post-selected Quantum Correlations from Classical Interference in a Multi-core Fiber Beamsplitter
arxiv-2101-04171.creator: J. Cariñe, M. Asan-Srain, G. Lima, S. P. Walborn
arxiv-2101-04171.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by J. Cariñe, M. Asan-Srain, G. Lima, S. P. Walborn. Fourth-order interference is an information processing primitive for photonic quantum technologies. When used in conjunction with post-selection, it forms the basis of photonic controlled logic gates, entangling measurements, and can be used to produce quantum correlations. Here, using classical weak coherent states as inputs, we study fourth-order interference in novel 4 × 4 4\times 4 multi-port beam splitters built within multi-core optical fibers.

arxiv-2108-07346.title: An Efficient Parallel Algorithm for finding Bridges in a Dense Graph
arxiv-2108-07346.creator: 1 st Ashwani Kumar, 2 nd Aditya Pratap Singh
arxiv-2108-07346.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by 1 st Ashwani Kumar, 2 nd Aditya Pratap Singh. This paper presents a simple and efficient approach for finding the bridges and failure points in a densely connected network mapped as a graph. The algorithm presented here is a parallel algorithm which works in a distributed environment. The main idea of our algorithm is to generate a sparse certificate for a graph and finds bridges using a simple DFS (Depth First Search).

arxiv-2204-01246.title: Angular dependence of the upper critical induction of clean s s - and d x 2 − y 2 d_{x^{2}-y^{2}} -wave superconductors with self-consistent ellipsoidal effective mass and Zeeman anisotropies
arxiv-2204-01246.creator: Aiying Zhao, Qiang Gu, Richard A. Klemm
arxiv-2204-01246.description: Abstract We employ the Schrödinger-Dirac method generalized to an ellipsoidal effective mass anisotropy in order to treat the spin and orbital effective mass anisotropies self consistently, which is important when Pauli-limiting effects on the upper critical field characteristic of singlet superconductivity are present.

arxiv-2206-10192.title: LDD: A Dataset for Grape Diseases Object Detection and Instance Segmentation
arxiv-2206-10192.creator: Leonardo Rossi*, Marco Valenti*, Sara Elisabetta Legler, Andrea Prati
arxiv-2206-10192.description: Abstract The Instance Segmentation task, an extension of the well-known Object Detection task, is of great help in many areas, such as precision agriculture: being able to automatically identify plant organs and the possible diseases associated with them, allows to effectively scale and automate crop monitoring and its diseases control.

arxiv-2208-02232.title: GAS: Generating Fast and Accurate Surrogate Models for Autonomous Vehicle Systems
arxiv-2208-02232.creator: Keyur Joshi, Chiao Hsieh, Sayan Mitra, Sasa Misailovic
arxiv-2208-02232.description: Abstract . Modern autonomous vehicle systems use complex perception and control components. These components can rapidly change during development of such systems, requiring constant re-testing. Unfortunately, high-fidelity simulations of these complex systems for evaluating vehicle safety are costly. The complexity also hinders the creation of less computationally intensive surrogate models.

arxiv-2305-07198.title: Model Predictive Control of Smart Districts Participating in Frequency Regulation Market: A Case Study of Using Heating Network Storage PubID: pubid:
arxiv-2305-07198.creator: Hikaru Hoshino, T. John Koo, Yun-Chung Chu, Yoshihiko Susuki
arxiv-2305-07198.description: Abstract Flexibility provided by Combined Heat and Power (CHP) units in district heating networks is an important means to cope with increasing penetration of intermittent renewable energy resources, and various methods have been proposed to exploit thermal storage tanks installed in these networks.

arxiv-2312-03709.title: UID as a Guiding Metric for Automated Authorship Obfuscation This research was conducted at Pennslyvania State University through an NSF funded REU. The entire research and paper creation process took eleven weeks, starting in late May of 2023 and ending early August 2023.
arxiv-2312-03709.creator: Nicholas Abegg
arxiv-2312-03709.description: Abstract Protecting the anonymity of authors has become a difficult task given the rise of automated authorship attributors. These attributors are capable of attributing the author of a text amongst a pool of authors with great accuracy. In order to counter the rise of these automated attributors, there has also been a rise of automated obfuscators.

arxiv-2404-15227.title: tsbootstrap : Enhancing Time Series Analysis with Advanced Bootstrapping Techniques
arxiv-2404-15227.creator: Sankalp Gilda sankalp.gilda@gmail.com, Benedikt Heidrich benedikt.heidrich@sktime.net, Franz Kiraly franz.kiraly@sktime.net
arxiv-2404-15227.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Sankalp Gilda sankalp.gilda@gmail.com, Benedikt Heidrich benedikt.heidrich@sktime.net, Franz Kiraly franz.kiraly@sktime.net. In time series analysis, traditional bootstrapping methods often fall short due to their assumption of data independence, a condition rarely met in time-dependent data. This paper introduces tsbootstrap , a python package designed specifically to address this challenge. It offers a comprehensive suite of bootstrapping techniques, including Block, Residual, and advanced methods like Markov and Sieve Bootstraps, each tailored to respect the temporal dependencies in time series data.

arxiv-2412-10746.title: Finite asymptotic dimension and the coarse assembly map
arxiv-2412-10746.creator: Ulrich Bunke
arxiv-2412-10746.description: Abstract In this note we give a simple argument for the fact that the coarse assembly map for a strong coarse homology theory with weak transfers and a bornological coarse space of weakly finite homotopical asymptotic dimension is a phantom equivalence.

arxiv-2501-06494.title: TopoFormer : Integrating Transformers and ConvLSTMs for Coastal Topography Prediction
arxiv-2501-06494.creator: Santosh Munian, Oktay Karakuş, William Russell, Gwyn Nelson Cardiff University, School of Computer Science and Informatics, CF24 4AG, UK Wales Coastal Monitoring Centre, Alps Depot, Wenvoe, CF5 6AA, UK
arxiv-2501-06494.description: Abstract This paper presents TopoFormer , a novel hybrid deep learning architecture that integrates transformer-based encoders with convolutional long short-term memory (ConvLSTM) layers for the precise prediction of topographic beach profiles referenced to elevation datums, with a particular focus on Mean Low Water Springs (MLWS) and Mean Low Water Neaps (MLWN).

arxiv-2502-11457.title: Aligning Sentence Simplification with ESL Learner’s Proficiency for Language Acquisition
arxiv-2502-11457.creator: Guanlin Li, Yuki Arase, Noël Crespi
arxiv-2502-11457.description: Abstract Text simplification is crucial for improving accessibility and comprehension for English as a Second Language (ESL) learners. This study goes a step further and aims to facilitate ESL learners’ language acquisition by simplification. Specifically, we propose simplifying complex sentences to appropriate levels for learners while also increasing vocabulary coverage of the target level in the simplifications.

arxiv-2509-00364.title: 3D Simulations of Convective Entrainment in Gas Giants: Rotation and Decreasing Luminosity as Barriers to Mixing
arxiv-2509-00364.creator: Shu Zhang (张舒), J. R. Fuentes, Andrew Cumming
arxiv-2509-00364.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Shu Zhang (张舒), J. R. Fuentes, Andrew Cumming. Observations from Juno and Cassini suggest that Jupiter and Saturn may possess fuzzy cores – central regions where the abundance of heavy elements varies smoothly with depth. Such gradients pose a longstanding puzzle for models of planetary evolution and formation, which predict that vigorous convection would homogenize the interior of gas giants within the first ∼ 10 6 \sim 10^{6} – 10 8 ​ years 10^{8}~\mathrm{years} of cooling.

arxiv-2509-06670.title: On Catastrophicity of Convolutional Codes and their encoders over ℤ p r {\mathbb{Z}}_{p^{r}}
arxiv-2509-06670.creator: Mohammed El Oued
arxiv-2509-06670.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mohammed El Oued. This paper investigates the existence of minimal p p -encoders for convolutional codes over ℤ p r \mathbb{Z}_{p^{r}} , where p p is a prime. This addresses a conjecture from [ 7 ] , which posits that every such code admits a minimal p p -encoder, implying that all convolutional codes over ℤ p r \mathbb{Z}_{p^{r}} are noncatastrophic when input sequences are restricted to coefficients in { 0 , … , p − 1 } \{0,\dots,p-1\} .

pmc-10614446.title: Seroprevalence of Enterovirus D68 Infection among Humans: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-10614446.creator: Yingying Shi, Qinqin Ran, Xiaochen Wang, Lu Shi
pmc-10614446.description: IntroductionHuman enterovirus D68 (EV-D68), which belongs to enteroviruses of the small RNA family, is a type of enterovirus that can cause acute respiratory tract infection and central nervous system diseases. This study systematically analysed and summarized EV-D68 antibody studies in databases and identified the seropositivity rates of different regions, ages, and sexes.MethodsMeta-analysis was performed using STATA 16.0 software.

pmc-11375236.title: Alternatives to DPA and ethoxyquin for preventing the development of superficial scald in apples: A review
pmc-11375236.creator: Konstantinos Papoutsis
pmc-11375236.description: Apples are one of most economically important crops worldwide with a production of approximately 96 million tons in 2022. During postharvest storage, apple quality can decline due to the development of physiological disorders. Superficial scald is one of the main physiological disorders that develops in apples during cold storage and results in quality deterioration.

pmc-11378110.title: Dermatophytic disease: A rare case report
pmc-11378110.creator: Sara Ez-zaky, Kaoutar Imrani, Joud Boutatleb, Nabil Moatassim Billah, Ittimade Nassar
pmc-11378110.description: Dermatophytic disease is a rare condition, primarily described in North Africa. This orphan disease owes its name to Hadida and Schousboe. Although the pathophysiology remains poorly understood, it is often associated with immune deficiency and occurs in the context of high consanguinity, as in our case.

pmc-11427388.title: Effects of different exercise interventions on executive function in children with autism spectrum disorder: a network meta-analysis
pmc-11427388.creator: Yaoqi Hou, Yan Wang, Jiaqi Deng, Xiangqin Song
pmc-11427388.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundA large body of research has identified the positive effects of physical activity on children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD). However, the specific benefits of different types of sports on executive functioning in children with ASD remain unclear.

pmc-11518037.title: Measuring functioning and disability in Korea: comparing general and dedicated surveys using the ICF
pmc-11518037.creator: J Kim, M Selb, Y T Cho, W H Kim, C Sabariego
pmc-11518037.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundFunctioning is the third health indicator besides mortality and morbidity. Although Korea periodically collects functioning information, the functioning indicator has not been generated yet. This study aimed to evaluate how functioning information is currently collected in Korea’s health and disability surveys, especially in terms of comparability and comprehensiveness, using the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) as a reference framework.MethodsData sources included three health and disability surveys in Korea (Population and Housing Census, Korean National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey,

pmc-11603968.title: Assessment of dental clinics’ infection control function using a checklist during the COVID-19 pandemic
pmc-11603968.creator: Zahra Momeni, Hamid Mirshamsi, Nastaran Parviz, Mohammad Elyasifard
pmc-11603968.description: IntroductionThe heightened risk of COVID-19 transmission during dental procedures has been a major concern in dentistry. To curb the spread of the virus, breaking the chain of transmission is paramount. This study aimed to assess infection control function in dental clinics using a supervisory checklist developed specifically during the COVID-19 pandemic.

pmc-11631705.title: circUBE2G1 interacts with hnRNPU to promote VEGF-C-mediated lymph node metastasis of lung adenocarcinoma
pmc-11631705.creator: Yuting Li, Hui Chen, Yue Zhao, Qilu Yan, Lulu Chen, Qibin Song
pmc-11631705.description: BackgroundPatients with lymph node(LN)metastasis-positive Lung adenocarcinoma(LUAD)suffer from a significantly reduced five-year survival rate. Increasing evidence indicates circular RNAs(circRNAs)play crucial roles in regulating cancer progression. However, the specific regulatory mechanisms of circRNAs in the LN metastasis of LUAD have not been fully explored.

pmc-11651466.title: Predictors of active and recurrent bleeding in upper gastrointestinal angiodysplasia: Results from 10-year esophagogastroduodenoscopy of a tertiary center in Taiwan
pmc-11651466.creator: Meng-Chuan Lu, Tien-Yu Huang, Peng-Jen Chen, Hsuan-Wei Chen, Chih-Wei Yang, Jung-Chun Lin, Wei-Chen Huang, Hsuan-Hwai Lin, Yu-Lueng Shih, Tsai-Yuan Hsieh, Bao-Chung Chen
pmc-11651466.description: Upper gastrointestinal angiodysplasia (UGIA) is a unique mucosal vascular lesion that causes acute or recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding. Despite the increasing incidence of UGIA, the risk factors for bleeding in this condition remain unclear. We investigated the predictors of active and recurrent bleeding among patients with UGIA.

pmc-11668930.title: Should We Fear A Wave of Cancers After the COVID-19 Pandemic?
pmc-11668930.creator: Seyed Mohammad Javad Mortazavi, Seyed Alireza Mortazavi, James S Welsh, Lembit Sihver
pmc-11668930.description: hat nowadays we can expect to live much longer than our ancestors who lived a few generations back [ 2 ]. Given these considerations, It is widely believed that increased life span is the main reason cancer risk overall is rising [ 3 ].

pmc-12415957.title: Bioinspired wearable polymer microneedle patches: pioneering diabetic wound therapy for the horizon
pmc-12415957.creator: Shana Zhang, Meng Wei, Chengxin Luan, Bingbing Gao
pmc-12415957.description: Diabetic wounds present persistent challenges due to impaired healing, recurrent infection, oxidative stress, and dysregulated glucose metabolism. Bioinspired polymeric microneedle (MN) patches have emerged as multifunctional platforms capable of penetrating the stratum corneum to deliver therapeutics directly into the dermis, enabling glucose regulation, antimicrobial action, reactive oxygen species (ROS) modulation, and proangiogenic stimulation.

pmc-12533907.title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) can be a possible predictive factor of incident CKD: NAGALA cohort study
pmc-12533907.creator: Yuriko Ono, Kimiko Sakai, Takuro Okamura, Hiroshi Okada, Akihiro Obora, Takao Kojima, Masahide Hamaguchi, Michiaki Fukui, Anna Di Sessa, Anna Di Sessa, Anna Di Sessa
pmc-12533907.description: BackgroundA decade-long follow-up study identified metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) as an independent predictor for the onset of chronic kidney disease (CKD). In 2023, a Delphi consensus introduced the term metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) as an updated nomenclature.

pmc-12880942.title: Psychological Impact of Pulmonary Embolism: A Narrative Review
pmc-12880942.creator: Farooq Hyder, Hina Pervaiz, Mubeena Javid, Raveena B Bansari, FNU Karishma, Daya Kumari, Poonam Kumari, Ali Karim, Hari V Nenwani, Allah Warayo, FNU Dropati, Kishor Kumari, Muhammad Salman, Abida Parveen
pmc-12880942.description: Background: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a potentially life-threatening thromboembolic condition that demands urgent medical attention. While significant strides have been made in the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of PE, its long-term psychological consequences remain underexplored. Survivors often face considerable emotional and psychological challenges that can impair recovery and reduce quality of life.

pmc-12951536.title: Unilateral Pulmonary Artery Agenesis in an Adult: A Case Report and Review of Literature
pmc-12951536.creator: Madhuranjan J, Arun Karthick R, Shashank Kaushik
pmc-12951536.description: BackgroundUnilateral pulmonary artery agenesis (UPAA) is a rare congenital anomaly that may remain undiagnosed until adulthood, when patients present with exertional dyspnoea, recurrent respiratory infections, hemoptysis, or pulmonary hypertension.Case PresentationA 55‐year‐old female presented with exertional dyspnoea and hypoxemia. Clinical evaluation and echocardiography revealed pulmonary arterial hypertension, cor pulmonale with preserved left ventricular systolic function.

pmc-13239981.title: Multiple Genetic Origins of Non‐Native, Self‐Sustaining Rainbow Trout Oncorhynchus mykiss in Streams in Baden‐Württemberg, Germany
pmc-13239981.creator: J. Peter Koene, Arne Jacobs, Patrick Bartolin, Jan Baer, David Frei, Pascal Vonlanthen, Alexander Brinker
pmc-13239981.description: Introduced in the late 19th Century, Oncorhynchus mykiss (rainbow trout) has been stocked historically in streams throughout Baden‐Württemberg, Germany, and some populations have become self‐sustaining with unclear impact on native salmonid populations. We sampled 223 rainbow trout from 14 streams and 3 hatcheries, each with different levels of domestication, from which the streams are known to have been stocked.

pmc-13301145.title: Revisiting ventricular tachycardia ablation: insights into pulsed field energy. A systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective studies
pmc-13301145.creator: M I A Bistriceanu, O Makdah, A M Buzarnescu, C G Ursu, C M Ciuciureanu, A Deaconu, R G Vatasescu
pmc-13301145.description: BackgroundRadiofrequency (RF) ablation remains the cornerstone of ventricular tachycardia (VT) therapy, yet its success is hindered by limited lesion depth in scarred myocardium and the risk of collateral thermal injury. Pulsed field ablation (PFA), inducing irreversible electroporation, may overcome these barriers by achieving deeper and more homogeneous lesions while preserving adjacent structures.

pmc-13346485.title: Age-related differences in whole-body muscle synergies during overarm throwing in children
pmc-13346485.creator: Takuya Murakami, Ayane Kusafuka, Taishi Okegawa, Daiki Yamasaki, Yuto Sakakibara, Nadaka Hakariya, Naotsugu Kaneko, Hiroki Saito, Atsushi Sasaki, Kimitaka Nakazawa
pmc-13346485.description: Overarm throwing is a uniquely human skill that requires precise whole-body coordination. Although throwing behavior emerges early in childhood, the neuromuscular mechanisms that support its development remain poorly characterized. Here, we provide novel evidence for the age-related differences of whole-body muscle synergies during maximum-effort throwing in preschool-aged (PS) and school-aged (SA) children.

pmc-13385646.title: Development and Assessment of Tailored Illustrations to Enhance Community Understandings of Genetics Topics
pmc-13385646.creator: Audrey M. Arner, Tobias C. McCabe, Amanda Seyler, Siti Nurani Zamri, Tan Bee Ting A/P Tan Boon Huat, Kar Lye Tam, Patriciah Kinyua, Echwa John, Sospeter Ngoci Njeru, Yvonne A. L. Lim, Michael Gurven, Colin Nicholas, Julien Ayroles, Vivek V. Venkataraman, Thomas S. Kraft, Ian J. Wallace, Amanda J. Le
pmc-13385646.description: ObjectivesEffective communication about genetics concepts is essential for collaborative anthropological genetics research. However, communication can be challenging because many ideas are abstract and are especially unfamiliar to communities with limited access to formal education. Indeed, there are no widely adopted models for communicating such information, nor a clear understanding of the social factors that may shape engagement.

pmc-13581770.title: Mechanisms and therapeutic insights from zebrafish models of wound healing
pmc-13581770.creator: Chengen Feng, Runxiang Li
pmc-13581770.description: Wound healing is essential for tissue integrity, yet chronic wounds remain a significant clinical challenge. The zebrafish (Danio rerio) offers unique advantages for studying wound repair: optical transparency enables real-time in vivo imaging, robust regenerative capacity allows scarless tissue restoration, and genetic tractability facilitates mechanistic dissection.
